name: Developer Platform (API, Webhooks, SDK, MCP)
description: External developer capabilities: API keys/OAuth clients, webhooks, event delivery guarantees, SDK conventions, and integration governance. Includes MCP (Model Context Protocol) guidance for safe tool exposure.
goals: Secure, scoped API access for third-party integrations.
Reliable webhook delivery with retries, signatures, and idempotency.
Clear versioning and deprecation strategy for APIs.
Tenant-safe developer experiences that prevent cross-workspace data access.
MCP readiness: expose approved tools/resources via a hosted MCP endpoint (SSE) backed by FastAPI + FastMCP reference architecture.

rules: API credentials are scoped to a workspace_id and a permission set.
Webhook endpoints are workspace-scoped and only receive workspace events.
All integration requests must pass workspace middleware and RBAC-equivalent checks.

actors.name: Workspace Admin
actors.description: Creates API keys/webhooks and grants scopes.

actors.name: MCP Client
actors.description: LLM app/agent using MCP to discover tools/resources and call them within a single workspace scope.

actors.name: System
actors.description: Signs webhooks, retries delivery, enforces scopes.

apis.notes: Hosted MCP endpoint. Recommended transport is Server-Sent Events (SSE) over HTTPS. Credentials must be scoped to a single workspace_id and a scope set. Tool/resource exposure is allowlisted and deny-by-default.

workflows.name: Webhook Delivery and Retry
steps: Domain emits OutboundEvent with stable event_id.
For each enabled WebhookEndpoint subscribed to event type, create WebhookDelivery attempt=1.
Send HTTPS POST with signature header (HMAC over timestamp + body).
On 2xx mark sent; otherwise schedule exponential backoff retries with jitter.
Provide replay tooling to workspace admins; never replay without audit logging.

controls: API keys stored hashed; show only once.
Scopes map to permissions; enforce at middleware.
Webhook signing secret stored in KMS/Vault.
SSRF protection: validate webhook URLs (no link-local, no private IP ranges) and enforce allowlists for enterprise.
MCP tool allowlisting: expose only approved tools/resources; deny-by-default; optionally require workspace admin enablement.
MCP tenancy enforcement: all MCP calls must bind to exactly one workspace_id and must be rejected if the credential workspace scope mismatches.
MCP scope enforcement: each tool/resource requires explicit scopes; do not infer broad access from role names.
MCP rate limiting: apply per workspace and per credential; consider stricter limits for expensive tools (AI/processing).

alerts: High webhook failure rate for a workspace

acceptanceTests: API keys cannot be retrieved in plaintext after creation.
Webhook signatures validate and reject tampered payloads.
Webhook retries follow backoff and stop after max attempts, surfacing failure in UI.
MCP endpoint requires authentication and rejects invalid/expired credentials.
MCP endpoint enforces workspace scoping (cannot access another workspace by changing workspace_id in the URL).
MCP tools/resources are deny-by-default and only appear when allowlisted/enabled for the credential scopes.
MCP tool calls are rate-limited and audited (tool name, workspace_id, credential id, status, latency).
